text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents for evaluation of a nonhealing right heel diabetic foot ulcer, referred by primary care.
- history of present illness: a blister from tight shoes about six weeks ago became unroofed, with foul odor, yellow drainage, and now blackening around the wound. Started oral antibiotics about six days ago with initial improvement, then worsening with chills, low-grade fever, calf cramping, and a red streak up the ankle and inner calf. Blood glucose has trended in the 300s to 400s for two weeks, with one reading of 500–600. Hiking about three to four days before symptom onset may have contributed.
- physical examination: slight fever with otherwise stable vitals. Right heel necrotic ulcer about 2 x 2 cm with sloughing, surrounding cellulitis and erythema, and odor. No bony exposure. Femoral and popliteal pulses palpable bilaterally; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses non-palpable but present by Doppler. Tenderness absent on direct wound palpation. Right foot X-ray shows no osteomyelitis.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: throbbing foot pain, calf pain and hardness with pain radiating to the knee, cough and dyspnea for two days, chills, low-grade fever, foul odor, blackening of the wound margin, red streaking up the leg.
- new medications prescribed or changed: continue the current antibiotic prescribed by primary care (about 10–12 day total course, roughly 2–3 days remaining); possible change or extension pending wound culture results. Dosage: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: wound culture pending; vascular blood flow test ordered; in-office debridement performed; return visit in seven days; follow up with endocrinologist; keep hemoglobin A1c below 7 and closely monitor blood sugars.
